clue.text: Relaxed with a book about Southend

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
read as South-end: the end letter of the word South

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a novel about the Essex seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend, an Essex seaside resort, is split as 'South end', giving its last letter H, which 'about' puts inside TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and comfortable is the idiomatic sense of feeling at ease in one's own house.

clue.text: Move on, with vertigo starting, in a knees-up

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a knees-up is a British term for a lively party with dancing

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of vertigo

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward dizzily at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party or dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to go forward or move on.

clue.text: Pussyfoot around hospital boundary

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an edge is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes around the edge of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' belongs with 'Pussyfoot' in the definition, not as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing oneself, to evade or dither.

clue.text: Miss Gabler, top half hidden, in a scarf

parts.note: to muff is to miss a catch or bungle it

indicators.note: in a down clue the top half of the name is its first three letters, which are removed

explanation.surface: Miss Gabler wears a scarf hiding the upper half of her face.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedda Gabler is Ibsen's heroine; in a down clue 'top half hidden' drops GAB, leaving LER.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is a warm scarf worn round the neck.

clue.text: Father takes on arbitrators in quarrel

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which settles labour disputes

explanation.surface: A priest steps in among mediators during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is a British public body that mediates in industrial disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl, a close synonym for a quarrel.

clue.text: I'm hers when bewitched in France

indicators.note: bewitched means put under a spell and transformed, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: A woman under a spell in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place clue 'in France': Rheims is a city in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, the cathedral city of Champagne, is a place located in France.

clue.text: Hear the promise — that's the slogan

parts.note: to catch something is to hear it
giving your word is giving a promise

explanation.surface: Listen to the pledge: it is the motto.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a phrase taken up as a slogan.

clue.text: Where children play and spit outside

indicators.note: outside means one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: Kids spit and play in the playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a playground enclosure filled with sand for children.

clue.text: A hem one should repair: everyone knows that

indicators.note: to repair is to mend, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A domestic sewing job everybody recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' reads as mending the hem but signals an anagram of A HEM ONE SHOULD.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or brand known in every home is famous, someone familiar to all.

clue.text: Enthusiastic singer makes a comeback

indicators.note: coming back is read as the word travelling backwards, right to left

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: An eager vocalist returns to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a comeback' reads like a career revival but signals that the singer's word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid is a direct synonym of enthusiastic, eager or keen.

clue.text: Italian takes the biscuit

definitions.meaning: a native of Florence, a city in Italy
a thin biscuit of nuts and fruit, often coated in chocolate

explanation.surface: An Italian man helps himself to the cookie, or wins the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being outrageous; here 'takes the' is just the link between two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person from Florence and a chocolate-backed nut biscuit.

clue.text: Sick one in Calais at the water hole

parts.note: un is French for one, and Calais is a French port
a well is a hole sunk to reach water

explanation.surface: A tourist falls ill in France beside the water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell is a plain synonym of sick or poorly.

clue.text: Woolly sheep moo? No chance at all!

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or vague, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fleecy sheep that lows like a cow? Impossible!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' looks like a description of the sheep but signals an anagram of SHEEP MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said ironically to mean there is little or no prospect at all.

clue.text: Refined actress and child seen in short reel

indicators.note: the pieces are seen inside, contained in the other word
short means cut, so the word reel loses its last letter

parts.note: Cher is the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A sophisticated film star and her offspring appear in a brief clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' turns REEL into REE, and CHER plus CH go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché means exquisite or rarefied, a loan from French used for something refined.

clue.text: Box the fodder and go to bed

parts.note: to box is to hit someone
hay is dried grass fed to animals

explanation.surface: Someone packs the animal feed and then turns in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to retire for the night, to sleep.

clue.text: Cover for one lying in child's bed

indicators.note: lying in means resting inside, so one piece is placed within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a baby's or small child's bed
a is used for one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Something to cover a person lying in a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is an outer covering, of a garment or of paint.

clue.text: Fortune for female put away

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A woman's luck hangs on what she stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate and fortune are both destiny, what chance holds in store.

clue.text: Supposed to be desired

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to imagine or suppose and to want or be attracted to.

clue.text: Danes pull out completely

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Scandinavians withdraw fully from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal for DANES PULL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes covering every extremity, meaning thoroughly or in every respect.

clue.text: Yesterday's writers finally made a loss

parts.note: ex means former, of yesterday
pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of made

explanation.surface: Writers of the past ended up losing money.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost, money paid out and so lost.

clue.text: Most terrible glue: it's coming unstuck

indicators.note: coming unstuck means falling apart, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the apostrophe is no letter, leaving ITS

explanation.surface: The worst adhesive is failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliest is the superlative of ugly, meaning most unpleasant or nasty.

clue.text: Fly that is swallowed, preserving the Roman way

indicators.note: preserving means keeping something safe inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: swallowed food means ate it
via is Latin for road or way

explanation.surface: An insect is eaten, keeping to the Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect being swallowed but is the verb meaning to pilot an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to fly an aircraft.

clue.text: Bearded nuns have put leader last

indicators.note: the leading letter of the phrase is moved to its end

explanation.surface: Nuns with beards are told their head must go to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Write NUNSHAVE and move its first letter N to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearded face is one that has not been shaved, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Two daughters in white splash about

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: pale means whitish, lacking colour
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them give DD

explanation.surface: Two girls in white play in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is to wade or splash in shallow water.

clue.text: Idler: one needs a doctor

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy man claims he needs to see a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, so a lazy person.

clue.text: Transport minister who said, "Stand and deliver!"?

definitions.text: Transport minister who said, "Stand and deliver!"?

parts.words: Transport minister who said, "Stand and deliver!"?
parts.note: a road robber of old is jokingly cast as a government official in charge of main roads

explanation.surface: A government transport chief barks a robber's demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand and deliver!' was the traditional demand of mounted robbers on English roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted robber of travellers on the open road is pictured as a man in charge of the roads.

clue.text: Warning given by last of Chicago guys

indicators.note: last of means take the final letter of the word Chicago

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: A tip-off comes from the final members of a Chicago gang.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a warning.

clue.text: Sofa back ready to drop through being gripped

indicators.note: back means read backwards, right to left
being gripped means held inside the other word

parts.note: someone ready to drop is dead tired, so dead
by means through, as in by means of

explanation.surface: Too exhausted to go on, someone collapses onto the couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sofa back' tempts you to reverse a word for sofa, but 'back' acts on the whole wordplay: 'being gripped' builds DEBYAD, which 'back' reverses; 'ready to drop' means dead tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A daybed is a couch that doubles as a bed, a kind of sofa.

clue.text: Feel bitter about being posted twice?

definitions.meaning: to take offence at or begrudge something

explanation.surface: Someone resents having a letter posted to them twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to be aggrieved at, and split as re-sent it means mailed again.
